source.title: Latent Communication Between Language Model Agents: Channels, Alignment, and the Limits of Text

record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-architecture representational alignment with Procrustes retrieval and related measures, rather than the original claim’s scaling comparison.
record.gate_note: The study tests cross-architecture alignment between two language models. It does not test whether alignment rises as model size or capability increases, cross-modal vision-language alignment, convergence across random seeds, or recurring interpretable features. The paper also reports channel-fidelity, SAE feature-survival, task-level, augmentation, and injection results; these do not directly measure the claim versions cataloged here.
record.test_reason: The study fits an orthogonal Procrustes map, plus CCA and MLP diagnostics, between Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct and Mistral 7B hidden states on anchor concepts. It measures held-out retrieval, cosine and probe transfer, which bears directly on V4. It also varies anchor count and alignment method, which bears on V6, and reports how complete the alignment is (V7). There is one model pair and no scale sweep, seeds, vision models or cross-model feature matching, so V1, V2, V3 and V5 are untested. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that cross-architecture convergence is real: 92% Procrustes top-1 at 140 anchors, with CCA 100% in a low-rank subspace. They attribute it to both models capturing the same distributional properties of language. The text channel matches or beats the latent channel by 3–10 pp on every task, and augmentation gives no benefit. The authors read the features lost by text as surface form, giving a negative result for their latent-advantage hypothesis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cross-architecture Procrustes retrieval and task-level communication tests rather than a scale sweep of representational similarity across independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieval changes with anchor count; CCA and Procrustes give different retrieval results; the MLP alignment fails; base Mistral v0.1 aligns slightly better than instruction-tuned v0.3; prompt averaging narrows the English task-level gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Within Llama, re-encoding a concept as its bare name instead of in context replaces about 88% of active SAE features (Jaccard 5.8%). The lost features are attributed to surface form.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one model, the SAE features active for a concept depend strongly on the input context, so feature identity is input-dependent rather than concept-fixed.

record.problems: The main cross-architecture comparison involves only one Llama–Mistral pairing. The maximum Procrustes anchor set leaves only 25 holdout concepts, and uncertainty estimates for retrieval are not reported. The study does not vary model scale or capability, and the attribution to shared training statistics is not causally tested.

untested.parts: No size or capability sweep; there is a single Llama–Mistral pair of about 8B parameters.
No vision–language pair. Cross-modal alignment is proposed only as future work.
Mapping without paired data, layer stitching and relative representations are untested. Only paired anchor concepts at one layer per model are used.
SAE features are compared only within Llama (text round-trip), not across models.
No comparison of representational similarity metrics (e.g. CKA, mutual kNN) or out-of-distribution inputs. Only alignment method and anchor count vary.

There is no test of whether shared training data or objectives cause the alignment. The authors assert this, and the base-vs-instruct comparison is only suggestive. No plateau with model scale is tested.

missing.what: Attribute and sense disambiguation, 112 tasks: dense latent 67.0% and SAE latent 67.9% versus text-passage 76.8% (no-comm 25.9%). The mapping costs about 10 pp.
Cross-lingual sense disambiguation, 33 tasks: mapped dense latent 51.5% versus text-passage 75.8%. The Procrustes map fitted on English anchors fails to preserve sense.
Base v0.1 aligns better than instruct v0.3 at every anchor count; only the 140-anchor value is recorded.

record.verdict_notes: There is a single model pair at one layer each, with small holdout sets (25 at 140 anchors) and no retrieval uncertainty. Most of the paper's results (channel fidelity, feature survival, augmentation, Gemma injection) are about communication channels within or between models, not convergence. The authors' 'Platonic' interpretation from the base-vs-instruct gap is not a causal test.

versions.untested_parts: No size or capability sweep; only one Llama–Mistral model pairing is compared.
No vision-language model pair or image-caption alignment test. Cross-lingual language tasks are not cross-modal tests.
No comparison across random initializations of the same architecture.
Tests learned Procrustes alignment with paired anchor concepts; does not test alignment without paired data, layer stitching, or relative representations.
Does not test whether the same interpretable features or circuits recur across different models.
Varies anchor count and compares Procrustes with CCA and an MLP, but does not systematically compare alternative similarity metrics or out-of-distribution inputs.

Reports alignment completeness under several methods and describes shared language-distribution statistics as an explanation, but does not manipulate training data or objectives to establish the cause.

relationships.condition: Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct → Mistral 7B (base v0.1 and instruct v0.3), linear maps with ≥100 anchors
relationships.reason: Procrustes held-out top-1 reaches 84.6–92% versus 0.87% chance (r3–r5), and top-5 reaches 96.9–100% (r8–r10). Instruct v0.3 reaches 88% (r19) and CCA 100% (r20). Alignment survives the SAE bottleneck (r18), and cross-lingual task accuracy matches text (r27).
relationships.display_finding: Procrustes achieved held-out top-1 retrieval of 84.6–92% versus 0.87% chance and top-five retrieval of 96.9–100%; instruct Mistral reached 88%, CCA reached 100%, alignment survived the SAE bottleneck, and cross-lingual accuracy matched text.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct → Mistral 7B (base v0.1 and instruct v0.3), linear maps with ≥100 anchors
source_check.reason: r3–r5 and r8–r10 show high held-out retrieval; r19 extends this to instruction-tuned Mistral, and r27 shows task-level parity with text. The supplementary CCA result r20 uses 80 anchors, outside this condition.

relationships.condition: Few anchors, probe transfer, and task-level use of mapped vectors
relationships.reason: Top-1 is only 43.5% at 50 anchors (r1). Holdout cosine stays around 0.42–0.53 (r11–r15). Probe transfer is at chance with 2 prompts per concept and 60.5% with more (r22–r23). Mapped latents trail text on English concept identification (r24, r26), and per the text fall to 51.5% on cross-lingual sense tasks.
relationships.display_finding: Top-1 retrieval was 43.5% with 50 anchors, held-out cosine stayed around 0.42–0.53, and probe transfer rose from chance with 2 prompts per concept to 60.5% with more; mapped latents trailed text on English concept identification and reached 51.5% on cross-lingual sense tasks.

source_check.condition: Few anchors, probe transfer, and task-level use of mapped vectors
source_check.reason: r1 and r11–r15 show incomplete correspondence; r22–r23 show weak or chance probe transfer; r24 and r26 trail native text representations. These results qualify interchangeability by fitting data and evaluation.

relationships.condition: Procrustes vs CCA, and anchor count, on the same model pair
relationships.reason: Measured retrieval moves from 43.5% to 92% with anchor count (r1–r5). At 80 anchors CCA gives 100% versus Procrustes 75.3% (r2, r20), so the measured degree depends on method and fitting set. The MLP failure (r21) is attributed to overfitting, not to absence of convergence.
relationships.display_finding: Retrieval increased from 43.5% to 92% as anchor count changed, and at 80 anchors CCA reached 100% versus 75.3% for Procrustes; the authors attributed MLP failure to overfitting.

relationships.display_finding: Holdout cosine after rotation plateaued near 0.53, whereas CCA retrieval reached 100%, making apparent completeness depend on the measure.
